artifact.summary: Closed red-green. role_coverage now re-runs each defect-scoped sign-off's test before letting a phase close, so a build cannot finish while the defect QA proved is still reproducing; with no repository to verify in it blocks rather than passing. Extracted covered_roles as the single definition of freshness -- coverage and the loop's role picker had diverging copies, so QA was counted as covered and re-issued at the same time. next() now reports 'blocked' when every role has signed but the defect persists, instead of raising StopIteration.

artifact.attack_path: Council.next() (src/charter/loop/machine.py:103) unconditionally calls role_coverage() on every poll from any role, with no authentication and no rate limit -- 'next' is the routine status call every role in the loop makes continuously. role_coverage() (src/charter/gates/checks.py:153-169) re-runs every still-fresh defect-scoped FailingTest signoff by calling validate_failing_test() (src/charter/contracts/validators.py:97), which shells out to `python -m pytest <test_path>::<test_name>` against self.repo -- the LIVE working tree, not the tree_sha pinned on the original signoff. Containment only checks that test_path resolves inside the repo and exists (_resolve_inside); it never inspects file content or re-verifies the file is unchanged since acceptance. So: (1) qa submits a FailingTest for tests/test_x.py::test_y, it genuinely fails, and is accepted; (2) before the phase closes, that file (or a conftest.py it imports) is edited on disk -- by a compromised dependency step, another role, or anyone with write access to the tree -- to add module-level or fixture code that does something malicious, while the target test still exits 1 so validate_failing_test still accepts the run as 'still failing'; (3) pytest's collection phase imports that module and executes the injected code with the full privileges of the charter process; (4) this re-executes on EVERY subsequent next() call from ANY role for as long as the defect stays open -- no new artifact, review, or sign-off is needed to trigger it, and a caller who innocently polls next() becomes the unwitting executor. The change moved test execution from a one-time, reviewed submission-time event into an unbounded, unauthenticated, TOCTOU-vulnerable side effect of a read-shaped status call.
